newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker, digests grind data.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker, digests grind data.

text.p: London cocoa futures pared losses at the close on Thursday but retained their bearish tone amid an uninspiring set of European quarterly grind results.

The UK fourth quarter grind, which came in 3.3 percent lower against the 1995 period at 45,147 tonnes, received a muted reaction after the market had been dragged down by speculative and origin sales earlier.
Forecasts were for a decline of around five percent.
The lower grind was due to a temporary slowdown in one of Mars's processing plants after a possible overgrinding the year before, industry sources said.
Traders were puzzled however by a steep 21.2 percent drop in German grind which kindled talk about possible inaccuracies in German data.
"Perhaps we should use imports of processed products and beans instead of grindings to look at consumption," said one.

Thursday's session saw an early spate of speculative selling as funds continued to build short positions. Ivorian shippers were also offering cocoa while trade houses appeared on both sides of the market.

The benchmark March position partially recovered from a session low of 865 stg -- a new contract low and 17-month low based on a second-month continuation basis -- ending at 872 stg a tonne, down seven. May shed eight to 892.
Industry buyers were largely absent, awaiting further falls to replenish stocks.
"I think they do have cocoa to buy but with prices at 17 month lows you can't afford to relax a bit," said one.
Volume totalled a healthy 9,709 lots including some switch activity. Trades said the March/May spread had risen to 22 stg from 20.
